newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends down on big-cap selling.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends down on big-cap selling.

text.p: Jakarta index ended down 1.42 percent on Thursday on foreign-led selling of big-capitalised stocks amid weak market sentiment after a series of recent sharp falls, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 9.26 points to 641.62 points. Total turn-over was 309 billion rupiah compared with 534 billion rupiah on Wednesday.
Decliners led advancers by 106 to 23 as 44 issues remained unchanged.
"Sentiment remained cautious after a series of recent sharp falls. The impacts of last night's rumours that the president was not well still lingered despite the denials," one broker said.
Palace sources denied rumours on Wednesday night that President Suharto was not well and said the president had a full schedule on Thursday. But brokers said the rumours further dampened sentiment.
State-controlled firms Telkom, bank BNI, and tin miner Tambang Timah remained among the heavy losers following the weak sentiment, brokers said.
"The rumours on the president's health further dampened sentiment and added another uncertainty into the market after Telkom's monopoly issues," another broker said.
Telkom fell 75 rupiah to 3,525 rupiah in moderate trading.
Telkom had denied recent market talk that a possible competitor linked to President Suharto's brother-in-law was likely to emerge and may end Telkom's monopoly ahead of schedule.
Brokers said local buying of selected Lippo stocks including Lippo Life, Lippo Bank and Multipolar helped limit the fall in the index.
